title: The perverse t-structure on a smooth curve and its heart
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $C$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension one. Work in $D^b_c(C,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with its standard constructible cohomology and truncations as in [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]. Use the support and perverse-class formulas of [def-per-support-condition, def-per-perverse-subcategories], interpreted at these rational coefficients: $\operatorname{SuppCon}(K)$ means $\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i}K\le i$ for every integer $i$, and $\operatorname{CosuppCon}(K)=\operatorname{SuppCon}(D_CK)$ with $D_C=R\mathcal Hom(-,Ra_C^!\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ as in [lem-a1-qbar-curve-duality]. Empty support has dimension $-\infty$. “Sheaf” means a constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf in the standard heart, and “lisse” has the finite-coefficient-field meaning of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves].

For $C_0$ over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $C=C_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$, Weil objects mean the Frobenius pairs of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The descriptions (1) and (3), the basic objects (4), and the exact sequences (5) also hold for Weil pairs in the fixed-pair category of the geometric perverse heart; this category is abelian. In these Weil assertions all immersions and sheaves are defined over $k_0$, and their underlying geometric objects are used in the support conditions. The bounded t-structure assertion in (2) concerns the geometric derived category. A category of Frobenius pairs in a triangulated category is not here being given a triangulated structure.

A sheaf is *punctual* if its support is
a finite set of closed points. Let ${}^pD^{\le0}(C)$ and
${}^pD^{\ge0}(C)$ be the classes of [def-per-perverse-subcategories].

1. (*Description.*) For $K\in D^b_c(C,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$,
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(C)&\iff \mathcal H^aK=0\ (a>0)\ \text{and}\
   \mathcal H^0K\ \text{is punctual},\\
   K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(C)&\iff \mathcal H^aK=0\ (a<-1)\ \text{and}\
   \mathcal H^{-1}K\ \text{has no nonzero punctual subsheaf}.
   \end{aligned}
   $$
2. (*t-structure.*) The pair $\bigl({}^pD^{\le0}(C),{}^pD^{\ge0}(C)\bigr)$
   is a bounded t-structure on $D^b_c(C,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ in the
   sense of [def-weil-t-structure]. Its heart
   $$
   \mathrm{Perv}(C):={}^pD^{\le0}(C)\cap{}^pD^{\ge0}(C)
   $$
   (the perverse heart candidate of [def-per-perverse-subcategories]) is
   an abelian category.
3. (*The heart.*) $K\in\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ if and only if
   $\mathcal H^aK=0$ for $a\notin\{-1,0\}$, $\mathcal H^0K$ is punctual,
   and $\mathcal H^{-1}K$ has no nonzero punctual subsheaf.
4. (*Basic objects.*) If $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ is a dense open immersion
   and $\mathcal N$ is a lisse sheaf on $U$, then the ordinary sheaf direct image shifted by one,
   $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ (the middle extension convention of [def-wf-middle-extension]) lies in
   $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$. If $x$ is a closed point with inclusion $i_x$ and
   $E$ is a sheaf on $x$ (a finite-dimensional continuous
   representation of the Galois group, respectively of the Weil group,
   of $k(x)$), then $i_{x*}E$, placed in degree $0$, lies in
   $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$.
5. (*Exact sequences.*) For $P\in\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ the sequence
   $0\to(\mathcal H^{-1}P)[1]\to P\to(\mathcal H^0P)[0]\to0$ is exact in
   $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$. A short exact sequence $0\to Q\to P\to R\to0$ in
   $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ gives an exact sequence of sheaves
   $$
   0\to\mathcal H^{-1}Q\to\mathcal H^{-1}P\to\mathcal H^{-1}R
   \to\mathcal H^0Q\to\mathcal H^0P\to\mathcal H^0R\to0 .
   $$

proof.text: Use [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] for the bounded standard t-structure and exact restrictions throughout. By [sk-lem-coefficient-heart], a constructible sheaf on a curve is lisse on a dense open with finite closed complement, and constructible sheaves form an abelian category. For finitely many sheaves, intersect these opens; the complement is still a finite union of finite sets. This gives a common lisse open for all nonzero cohomology sheaves of any bounded constructible complex. A constructible sheaf has zero-dimensional support exactly when it is punctual: its support is a finite union of locally closed strata, and any stratum meeting a generic point contains an open subset of that one-dimensional component. Thus zero-dimensional support misses all component generic points; each of its finitely many strata has zero-dimensional closure. By [lem-sc-dim0-finite] these closures are finite sets of closed points. Conversely a finite closed support has dimension at most zero. A sheaf with empty support is zero, by open–closed vanishing detection after choosing the common stratification.

source.place: Step 1: stratification and the support condition

proof.text: A lisse sheaf $M$ on a smooth curve $V$ has no nonzero punctual subsheaf. Indeed, on each connected component remove the finite support of a putative subsheaf $G$, obtaining a dense open $v:V'\hookrightarrow V$. By [lem-sc-smooth-normal], smooth curves are normal; [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective](3) gives $M\cong v_*v^*M$. Under the ordinary adjunction of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], the inclusion $G\to M$ corresponds to a map $v^*G=0\to v^*M$, and is zero. Since it is monic, $G=0$. The conclusion also holds for Weil subsheaves after forgetting Frobenius.

source.place: Step 0(i): lisse sheaves have no punctual subsheaves; finite-stage dense restriction replaces the invalid étale trivialization of a rational local system

proof.text: Let $F$ be constructible and choose a dense lisse open $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ as in Step 1. Put $F_{\mathrm p}=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$. This kernel is constructible by the abelian closure of [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] and constructibility of $j_*j^*F$ from [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]; it vanishes on $U$ and hence is punctual. If $G\subset F$ is punctual, $j^*G\subset j^*F$ is a punctual subsheaf of a lisse sheaf and is zero by Step 2. Adjunction forces $G$ into $F_{\mathrm p}$. For a lisse $M$ on $U$, any map from a punctual $G$ to $j_*M$ is zero: its adjoint $j^*G\to M$ has punctual image, zero by Step 2. Thus $j_*M$ has no punctual subsheaf, and neither does $F/F_{\mathrm p}$, which embeds into $j_*j^*F$. This proves existence, maximality and the torsion-free quotient directly; no new node restates this argument.

source.place: Step 0(ii): maximal punctual subsheaf and its quotient

proof.text:
For a complex $N$, every support has dimension at most one. The inequality of [def-per-support-condition] for $i\ge1$ is automatic, for $i=0$ says that $\mathcal H^0N$ is punctual, and for $i<0$ says that $\mathcal H^{-i}N=0$. This proves the upper description in (1), using [def-per-perverse-subcategories]. If $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ makes all its cohomology lisse, with complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$, exact restriction and vanishing detection from [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], and Step 2, give
$$\operatorname{SuppCon}(N)\iff \mathcal H^a(j^*N)=0\ (a\ge0),\quad \mathcal H^a(i^*N)=0\ (a>0).\tag{*}$$
Indeed punctual lisse restrictions are zero, and a sheaf with zero restriction to $U$ is supported on the finite set $Z$.

source.place: Step 1: the support condition and formula (*)

proof.text:
By [lem-a1-qbar-curve-duality], the dualizing objects on $U$ and $Z$ are $\Lambda(1)[2]$ and $\Lambda$. Applied with $K=\Lambda$, [lem-per-dual-lisse-tensor] therefore gives $D_UM=M^\vee(1)[2]$ for lisse $M$ on $U$, and $D_ZM=M^\vee$ for a sheaf on $Z$. Here all constructible sheaves on the finite reduced zero-dimensional $Z$ are lisse. Dualizing a bounded complex with lisse cohomology consequently gives
$$\mathcal H^a(D_UN)\cong(\mathcal H^{-2-a}N)^\vee(1),\qquad \mathcal H^a(D_ZL)\cong(\mathcal H^{-a}L)^\vee.$$
For completeness, induct on the number of occupied cohomology degrees. The zero complex is immediate; for top degree $n$, dualize the standard triangle $N'\to N\to\mathcal H^nN[-n]\to$, where $N'=\tau^{\le n-1}N$. The first term of the dual triangle has its only cohomology in degree $-2-n$ (respectively $-n$ on $Z$), while by induction the third term has cohomology in strictly larger degrees. The long exact sequence gives the stated isomorphism in the first degree and the induction isomorphisms in every higher degree; all lower terms vanish. These long exact sequences and truncations are supplied by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1),(5), applied to the standard t-structure of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]. Linear dual of a finite-dimensional coefficient space detects zero, and the Tate line is invertible, so both formulas also detect vanishing.

source.place: Step 2: duals on U and Z; truncation induction made explicit

proof.text:
Choose a common lisse open for the cohomology of $K$. The comparisons of [lem-a1-qbar-curve-duality] identify $j^*D_CK$ with $D_Uj^*K$ and $i^*D_CK$ with $D_ZRi^!K$. Step 5 shows that this same open works for $D_CK$. Apply (*) to $D_CK$. On $U$, degrees $a\ge0$ of the dual correspond to degrees $-2-a\le-2$ of $j^*K$; on $Z$, degrees $a>0$ correspond to degrees $-a<0$ of $Ri^!K$. Thus
$$\operatorname{CosuppCon}(K)\iff j^*K\in D^{\ge-1},\quad Ri^!K\in D^{\ge0}.$$
This uses the rational coefficient comparison itself; the ambient finite-ring costalk lemma is not substituted for it.

source.place: Step 3: first paragraph and the cosupport criterion

proof.text:
Assume $j^*K\in D^{\ge-1}$. By [prop-sf-localization-all-stages](3), there is a constructible distinguished triangle
$$i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow .$$
By [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], the last term has no cohomology below $-1$, and its degree $-1$ cohomology is $j_*j^*\mathcal H^{-1}K$, with the cohomology map equal to the ordinary unit. Since $i_*$ is exact, the long exact sequence supplied by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](5) for the standard t-structure gives
$$i_*\mathcal H^b(Ri^!K)\cong\mathcal H^bK\quad(b\le-2),$$
$$0\to i_*\mathcal H^{-1}(Ri^!K)\to\mathcal H^{-1}K\to j_*j^*\mathcal H^{-1}K.$$
By Step 3 the last kernel is the maximal punctual subsheaf of $\mathcal H^{-1}K$. Full faithfulness of $i_*$ detects zero, so $Ri^!K\in D^{\ge0}$ is equivalent to vanishing of every $\mathcal H^bK$ for $b\le-2$ and absence of a nonzero punctual subsheaf of $\mathcal H^{-1}K$. Together with Step 6 this proves the lower description in (1).

source.place: Step 3: closed-support triangle, bottom cohomology and maximal punctual kernel

proof.text:
Write the shifted classes as in [def-per-perverse-subcategories]. The descriptions now proved show they are strictly full and satisfy the shift inclusions in [def-weil-t-structure](1). They also show $B\in{}^pD^{\ge1}$ precisely when $\mathcal H^bB=0$ for $b<0$ and $\mathcal H^0B$ has no punctual subsheaf. Let $A\in{}^pD^{\le0}$ and $B\in{}^pD^{\ge1}$. Standard truncation adjunctions, [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) for the bounded standard structure of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H^0A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H^0A,\mathcal H^0B).$$
The image of any such sheaf morphism is punctual, being a quotient of the punctual sheaf $\mathcal H^0A$. It is therefore zero inside $\mathcal H^0B$. This is the orthogonality axiom.

For arbitrary $K$, set $K'=\tau^{\le0}K$, $F=\mathcal H^0K$, and use its maximal punctual subsheaf $F_{\mathrm p}$ from Step 3. Complete $K'\to F[0]\to(F/F_{\mathrm p})[0]$ to a triangle $A\to K'\to(F/F_{\mathrm p})[0]\to$. By the long exact cohomology sequence, $\mathcal H^aA=\mathcal H^aK$ for $a<0$, $\mathcal H^0A=F_{\mathrm p}$ and $\mathcal H^aA=0$ for $a>0$. Hence $A\in{}^pD^{\le0}$. Apply the octahedral axiom to $A\to K'\to K$; the standard cone $\tau^{\ge1}K$ of $K'\to K$ yields triangles
$$A\to K\to B\to,\qquad (F/F_{\mathrm p})[0]\to B\to\tau^{\ge1}K\to.$$
The latter long exact sequence gives $\mathcal H^bB=0$ for $b<0$ and $\mathcal H^0B=F/F_{\mathrm p}$, which has no punctual subsheaf by Step 3. Thus $B\in{}^pD^{\ge1}$, the required truncation axiom of [def-weil-t-structure]. Cone completion and octahedra in this common-stage coefficient category are supplied by [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms]; the standard truncation maps and cohomology calculations use [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] and [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1),(5). This is a direct construction of the perverse truncation triangle, not an application of a lemma restating (2).

source.place: Step 4: construction of the truncation triangle using the punctual kernel and the octahedron

proof.text: If the standard cohomology of $K$ is in $[a,b]$, the two descriptions give $K\in{}^pD^{\le b+1}\cap{}^pD^{\ge a}$. Hence the new t-structure is bounded, as defined in [def-weil-t-structure]. Its heart is abelian by [prop-weil-heart-abelian]. Intersecting the upper and lower descriptions gives exactly (3), and proves (2).

source.place: Step 4: boundedness, abelianness and the heart description

proof.text: For a lisse $\mathcal N$ on $U$, [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] makes $j_*\mathcal N$ constructible. By Step 3 it has no punctual subsheaf, so $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ has exactly the allowed degree $-1$ cohomology. This is the ordinary direct-image convention in [def-wf-middle-extension], with the same explicit formula over a general perfect field. For a closed point $x$, exact closed direct image in [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] puts $i_{x*}E$ entirely in degree $0$, supported on $\{x\}$. Thus both belong to the heart by (3), proving (4).

For $P$ in the perverse heart, the standard truncation triangle is $(\mathcal H^{-1}P)[1]\to P\to(\mathcal H^0P)[0]\to$. Both outer terms are in the perverse heart by (3). Part (4) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], applied to the perverse t-structure, turns this into the claimed short exact sequence. Conversely any short exact sequence $0\to Q\to P\to R\to0$ in this heart extends to a distinguished triangle by that same part (4). Apply part (5) for the standard t-structure. Since all three complexes have cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$, its long exact cohomology sequence reduces exactly to
$$0\to\mathcal H^{-1}Q\to\mathcal H^{-1}P\to\mathcal H^{-1}R\to\mathcal H^0Q\to\mathcal H^0P\to\mathcal H^0R\to0.$$
The standard truncations used here are those of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology].

source.place: Step 6: exact sequences in the geometric heart

proof.text: For the Weil assertion, work on the geometric fiber $C$ of $C_0$. By [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], objects are Frobenius pairs and their morphisms are equivariant geometric morphisms. The cohomology and duality comparisons in [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology, lem-a1-qbar-curve-duality] commute with Frobenius; Frobenius is an isomorphism of schemes and preserves finite support. Hence it preserves both perverse classes and the geometric perverse heart. The category of its fixed pairs in that abelian heart is abelian: for an equivariant map, the kernel and cokernel in the geometric heart inherit unique Frobenius isomorphisms by their universal properties, and the equality of image and coimage is equivariant for the same reason. Kernels and cokernels are therefore computed after forgetting Frobenius. The descriptions (1),(3), basic objects (4), and the canonical standard-truncation short exact sequence in (5) carry Frobenius. For any short exact sequence of Weil perverse pairs, forget Frobenius and use Step 12 for its six-term cohomology sequence; its arrows are equivariant by functoriality. We have proved precisely these Weil assertions, without cone completion in a fixed-pair category.
